proof.text: Fix an arbitrary object $U\to V$ and set $E=K_1|_U$, $\mathcal O=k_U$. Restriction to the slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Applied to kernels and images in the cohomology formula [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], this gives $H^q(E)=H^q(K_1)|_U$. Hence $H^q(E)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The definition [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] supplies local constant finite-dimensional models for the remaining sheaves. The same models restrict to $\mathcal C/U$: a covering sieve pulls back to a covering sieve, and restriction is sectionwise on the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. In particular no exactness of evaluation on $U$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), exact restriction to a slice; the sectionwise cohomology calculation.

proof.text: Put $F_q=H^q(E)$. On each trivializing slice a basis of its finite-dimensional model identifies $F_q$ with $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$, so tensoring there sends a module $G$ to $G^{\oplus r}$ (the coordinate maps are $e_j\otimes g\mapsto (0,\ldots,g,\ldots,0)$). For a short exact sequence, restriction remains exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and tensor commutes with restriction by [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. Its tensor sequence is therefore exact on these slices, being a finite direct sum of the restricted sequence. This implies exactness globally: kernels are sectionwise, and a section in the kernel is locally in the image precisely when its class in the sheafified cokernel is locally zero; the sheaf axiom then makes that class zero [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $F_q$ is flat in the tensor-exact sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. This local finite-basis argument is an elementary step, not a separate node.

source.place: Tags 03ER (definition-flat), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), applied to the localization of Tag 03DH; finite-free tensor and local exactness from sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels.

proof.text: Choose a representing complex of $E$ and put $T_q=\tau_{\le q}E$. The canonical truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] are $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to F_q[-q]\to T_{q-1}[1]$. From the explicit truncation in that statement, $H^i(T_q)=H^i(E)$ for $i\le q$ and is zero for $i>q$: in degree $q$ the last term is $\ker d^q$, and the other degrees are unchanged or zero. Thus $T_{a-1}$ is acyclic and the inclusion $T_b\to E$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies $T_{a-1}$ with zero and $T_b$ with $E$.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), second displayed triangle, with its index a=q-1.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any $\mathcal O$-module sheaf, placed in degree zero. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to L[0]$ with $P$ K-flat and all terms flat. These are sheaves of modules over the commutative ring sheaf $\mathcal O$; their tensor is additive and symmetric by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], with direct-sum total complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The resolution and the resolving-class equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] supply the K-flat left-derivability hypotheses of [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated]. Consequently $QL\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$, where $QL=Q(P)=L[0]$, preserves distinguished triangles and shifts. Symmetry identifies this with $\Phi(-)=(-)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L[0]$: on homogeneous terms of degrees $r,s$ the comparison is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{rs}y\otimes x$; the total differential gives a chain map, whose inverse is the same interchange. Descent along the K-flat equivalence gives this comparison for derived objects. Thus $\Phi$ is exact and shift-compatible, and sends zero to zero.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor and the preceding exact-functor construction), and the signed symmetry immediately following 06YU.

proof.text: The single complex $F_q[-q]$ is bounded above and termwise flat by Step 2, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Both it and $P$ are therefore flat-term K-flat complexes, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] represents $\Phi(F_q[-q])$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(F_q[-q]\otimes_{\mathcal O}P)$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] its degree-$i$ term is $F_q\otimes P^{i-q}$ and its differential is $(-1)^q(1\otimes d_P)$. Tensoring with $F_q$ is exact, so it preserves kernels, images and their quotients; the cohomology formula [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] yields $H^i\Phi(F_q[-q])\cong F_q\otimes H^{i-q}(P)$. Since $P\to L[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, this vanishes unless $i=q$. This calculation uses no boundedness or flatness assumption on the arbitrary test sheaf $L$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), applied to the single flat sheaf; Tag 06YU for computation on K-flat complexes.

proof.text: Induct on the finite integer interval $a-1\le q\le b$. The claim is that $H^i\Phi(T_q)=0$ for $i<a$ or $i>q$; the base $q=a-1$ holds because $T_{a-1}=0$. For $a\le q\le b$, Step 4 sends the truncation triangle of Step 3 to a distinguished triangle. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains $H^i\Phi(T_{q-1})\to H^i\Phi(T_q)\to H^i\Phi(F_q[-q])$. If $i<a$ or $i>q$, the outer terms are zero by the induction hypothesis and Step 5, hence the middle term is zero by exactness. At $q=b$, $T_b\simeq E=K_1|_U$, giving the required vanishing outside $[a,b]$. Both $U$ and $L$ were arbitrary. The other hypotheses of the item specify its intended residue object; no step needs to strengthen them.

title: Flat bounded cohomology gives finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and its residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] weakly contractible for its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation on $V$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_V$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived complete for its coefficient quotient tower [def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $k_V$ for the constant sheaf of residue fields [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $K_1=K\otimes^L_B k_V$, the derived reduction modulo $\varpi$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] (here $k_V=(R/\varpi)_V$). Suppose $a\leq b$ are integers, $H^q(K_1)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and each $H^q(K_1)$ is locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-vector-space local models [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Then for every object $U\to V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, every sheaf $L$ of $k_U$-modules, and every $i\notin[a,b]$, one has
$$H^i\bigl((K_1|_U)\otimes^L_{k_U}L\bigr)=0,$$
where $k_U=k_V|_U$ and restriction is to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. Thus the residue complex has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ on every slice, not just after evaluation on $V$.
